title: Plan: one UI kit
description: A small set of parts every page and card is built from, browsed as a tree in the library, checked at merge without screenshots.

add.title: 1. Five card styles, as variants of one card
add.text:
The [library](/framework/library/?at=ui/card) gets five children under **card**, compact to large:

- **A** a card with an H3 title
- **B** cards stacked with no gap
- **C** icon rows, like a file tree
- **D** a compact list
- **E** today's large card

Each is a page under `ui/card/` whose `specimen` draws the real thing from `ui/card`, `ui/row`, `ui/item`, with **no new CSS** in the page. Where a look is missing, it is added once to the component's own css, not to the page. The draft on `draft/card-styles` is the starting point.

add.title: 2. Arrow keys in the library
3. A layout check at merge, no screenshots
add.text:
A new script measures each page a change touches, at 400 and 1200 wide, with the existing [DesignTool](/framework/ext/DesignTool/) and PaddingContract (numbers, no AI):

```
node Server/layout-check.mjs /live/plan/ui-kit/ /framework/library/
  400   BROKEN  text overflows its card (.live-card > p)
  1200  GOOD
```

`merge.mjs` runs it on the pages it already smoke-tests. **First version reports only**, and records each page's findings as its baseline. Phase 2 fails a merge that adds a new BROKEN. Screenshots stay for the owner's pick only.
Next, one step at a time

add.title: 4. The kit as a tree, from H1 up
add.text:
The library's **ui** collection becomes the template tree you described: elements first, then compositions.

```
elements    h1 h2 h3 h4 · p · li · link · icon · badge
parts       row · item · tree · controls · field
cards       card → its five styles (step 1)
menus       menu · tabs · toolbar
pages       a page template (core/Page/Template)
```

Each node is a page with an icon and its variants as `children`, so the file tree, the item tree and the library are the same tree.

add.title: 5. The rule: pages add no CSS
add.text:
Page and card code composes kit parts and adds no CSS of its own. A new look becomes a library variant first, then the page uses it.

Enforced by a count, not a reminder: `layout-check.mjs` also reports CSS lines a change adds outside `ui/` and `styles/`; phase 2 fails the merge on any.

add.title: 6. LivePage's cards move onto the kit
add.text: `public/live/LivePage.css` is 282 lines of its own styling. Its cards, rows and file lists move onto `ui/card`, `ui/row`, `ui/item` in small steps, one part per merge, alongside the [fold plan](/live/plan/fold/). The session view (/live/session/) already does this with no local CSS, and logs each gap it hits; those gaps are this step's list.

add.title: Alternatives, and why not
add.text:
- **Fail merges on BROKEN today.** Not first: nobody has measured how many pages are already BROKEN; failing now could block every merge. Report first, fail on *new* BROKEN next.
- **Screenshot every page at merge.** Costs tokens and fixes nothing, as you said. The numbers find the breakage; a shot is for choosing.
- **A new component system.** No: `ui/`, `styles/` and the library already exist. The gap is that nothing makes pages use them.

3-a-layout-check-at-merge-no-screenshots.title: 1. A layout check at merge, no screenshots
3-a-layout-check-at-merge-no-screenshots.text:
A new script measures each page a change touches with the existing [DesignTool](/framework/ext/DesignTool/) and PaddingContract (numbers, no AI), at the widths merge already picks per change (400 and 1200 at least):

```
node Server/LayoutCheck.mjs /live/plan/ui-kit/ /framework/library/
  400   BROKEN  text overflows its card (.live-card > p)
  1200  GOOD
```

`merge.mjs` runs it in the browser and on the worktree server it already uses for the smoke test. **First version reports only.** Each page's findings are kept in `Server/layout-baseline.jsonl`; phase 2 fails a merge that adds a new BROKEN. Screenshots stay for the owner's pick only.

Page and card code composes kit parts and adds no CSS of its own. A new look becomes a library variant first, then the page uses it.

Enforced by a count, not a reminder: `LayoutCheck.mjs` also reports CSS lines a change adds outside `ui/` and `styles/`. Report first; then fail only a merge that makes that count **grow** (LivePage.css alone is 282 lines today, so a hard fail would block every merge).
